text:
maria-cloud: Hey infra team — new customer pilot coming up, need to preflight a bunch of quotas and get a quick project approval. Project ID: redwood-pilot-conv-2026 (billing host: rw-billing-prod). Timeline: must be ready in ~2 weeks.

Request summary:
- GPUs: 8 x A100 (us-west1), 12 x H100 L4 (us-central1) as spot/burst pool, 16 x L4 (us-west1) for inference experiments
- Network: 50 ephemeral external IPs (customer whitelist for dedicated endpoints), bump egress to +10 Gbps in us-west1
- Other: enable Shared VPC attachment (rw-shared-vpc), service account pre-provisioning, and increase for forwarding rules / load-balancer quota as needed.

Why: this is a low-latency LLM inference pilot with burstable traffic patterns. We want spot burst pools to keep costs down but need capacity headroom and static-ish ephemeral IPs to satisfy customer allowlists. Can someone confirm the right quota names/values to request and whether we should use Cloud NAT instead of so many external IPs? Also, who can approve creating the GCP quota request and submitting it under rw-billing-prod?

james-enginfra: Thanks — a couple clarifying Qs: what's the expected sustained GPU hours per day and peak concurrency? Also, do we need all 50 external IPs at once or can we use fewer + NAT? And which region will carry production traffic (us-west1 vs us-central1)?

maria-cloud: Peak target ~5k qps across pools, sustained 30% utilization on avg. We expect spikes that need bursts ~2-3 hours/day. The 50 IPs are for per-customer dedicated egress endpoints (customers want distinct source IPs); could potentially reduce to 20 if we use a pool + NAT, but some customers require a dedicated IP. Primary region for low-latency customers is us-west1, us-central1 is for fallbacks and H100 capacity.

ritesh-sre: Quick notes from oncall perspective:+ We should avoid 50 static/external IPs if Cloud NAT can satisfy the allowlist requirements — NAT gives single or few IPs but loses per-customer segregation. + If customers insist on per-customer IPs, consider using regional internal load balancers + external forwarding rules; those consume forwarding-rule and addresses quotas.

ritesh-sre: Also please add the project numeric ID. GCP quota requests require billing-hostproject and numeric project id for the target.

maria-cloud: Numeric project id is 123456789012.

james-enginfra: Proposed quota numbers to submit (per-region):
- us-west1: A100 GPUs: 8 (accelerator quota: A100 or equivalent)
- us-central1: H100 L4: 12 (spot-preemptible/ephemeral)
- us-west1: L4: 16 (inference pool)
- addresses (regional, us-west1): 20 reserved ephemeral external IPs + 30 global ephemeral (fallback) — or, if we opt for NAT, drop to 5 static NAT IPs and request Cloud NAT egress bandwidth +10 Gbps
- forwarding-rules / backend-services bump: +30 rules

james-enginfra: For the GCP request form, use these quota fields: "GPUs (all)" / "NVIDIA A100" / "NVIDIA H100" / "NVIDIA L4" (name may vary), and "Static External IP addresses" (regional). When you fill the form include the service account used for deploy and the billing host project (rw-billing-prod).

maria-cloud: Noted. I'll trim the external IP ask to 30 and include a justification that some customers require unique egress IPs.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-4627: "redwood-pilot-conv-2026 GCP quota request". Link: https://tickets.internal/r/INFRA-4627

sarah-ops: From finance/ops: we need a cost estimate for sustained and peak month to sign off — can you attach expected monthly GPU hours (regular + spot), and confirm whether spot termination risk is acceptable for the pilot (SLA implications). Also cc: security for Shared VPC attachment.

maria-cloud: Will produce a short cost table and spot-failure mitigation plan by EOD. For cost roughs: expected sustained (30% util) ~= 8 A100 * 24 * 30 * 0.3 + 12 H100 spot * average 6 hours/day ~ I'll paste a proper table in the ticket.

james-enginfra: Preflight checklist for whoever submits the GCP form:
1) Confirm numeric project id and billing hostproject (done)
2) Confirm shared VPC attachment and request the hostproject admin to accept connection (rw-shared-vpc)
3) Add service account: svc-redwood-pilot@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com with roles compute.networkAdmin, compute.viewer for quota ops
4) Provide estimated monthly spend and reason (pilot, production target, SLA)
5) Note fallback plan: auto-fallback to lower-cost model variants or cross-region routing if quota denied

ritesh-sre: +1 on the checklist. Also add: request increase to 'Forwarding rule' quota and 'External IP addresses (regional)'. Include region names in the GCP form text fields.

maria-cloud: Thanks all — I'll update INFRA-4627 with numbers (A100:8, H100:12, L4:16, external IPs:30 regional us-west1, egress +10 Gbps) and attach the cost table/security notes. Can someone from infra (james/ritesh) verify the final form before submission?

james-enginfra: I can review once you dump the draft here. If security signs off, I approve submission.

ritesh-sre: I'll look at the networking bits. If we can reduce external IPs by using a mix of NAT + per-customer IPs we should, but approve form with justification.

maria-cloud: Perfect — will post the draft request in INFRA-4627 in ~2 hours. Thanks! :pray:
